stem:
Meena tests four colourless liquids found in her kitchen in Jaipur. She dips blue litmus paper and red litmus paper into each liquid and records what she sees.

Liquid P: blue litmus turns red, red litmus stays red.
Liquid Q: red litmus turns blue, blue litmus stays blue.
Liquid R: both papers keep their original colours.
Liquid S: blue litmus turns red, red litmus stays red.

Which liquid should Meena classify as basic?

options.text: Liquid P, because it changes the colour of one litmus paper.
Liquid Q, because it turns red litmus paper blue.
Liquid R, because it does not change either litmus paper.
Liquid S, because both papers stay red after testing.

teacher.key_rationale: A basic substance turns red litmus blue while leaving blue litmus unchanged; only Liquid Q shows this paired response, so the key is B. Liquids P and S turn blue litmus red (acidic), and Liquid R leaves both papers unchanged (neutral). Options A, C and D each misread the paired litmus evidence.
